title: Customer Insights - Data: MCP server grounds agents in unified customer profiles and insights
summary: The briefing's configuration, consent, security and billing statements are supported by Microsoft documentation. It accurately reports the roadmap targets while distinguishing them from the documented connection experience. One additional source should be cited for the add-on capacity wording.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agent usage is measured in Copilot Credits, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage. You calculate the total cost based on the sum of the Copilot Credits your organization uses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: No separate licence for the Customer Insights MCP server is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Customer Insights MCP server separate licensing price charge rate. Opened Customer Insights paid-license, mcp-server-tools, mcp-server-tools-reference and mcp-server-agent365-tooling-gateway; none states a separate MCP server licence.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: What is not published; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate charge or Customer Insights MCP-specific call rate is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Customer Insights MCP server separate licensing price charge rate. Opened the Customer Insights licensing and three MCP pages, Copilot Studio Billing rates and management, and Overview of usage-based billing; no Customer Insights MCP-specific rate found.

claims.claim: Employee-facing agent and invoked-tool use is included in Microsoft Copilot USL when its licensed user is authenticated and the agent uses that user's identity.
claims.quote: included in the Microsoft Copilot USL when the user of the agent is licensed with Microsoft Copilot, and the agent operates using the authenticated Microsoft Copilot USL user's identity.

claims.claim: The billing page states that generative answer responses incur charges outside its stated exception.
claims.quote: Agents incur charges for generative answer responses unless the agent is created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response doesn't leverage tenant graph grounding.

claims.claim: Billing rates and management describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: For Microsoft Copilot harness experiences, Copilot Credits are charged for tools including knowledge and MCPs.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: The Model Context Protocol server exposes Customer Insights capabilities as callable tools for agents and chat clients.
claims.quote: The Customer Insights Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data and select Customer Insights - Journeys capabilities as callable tools for LLM agents.

claims.claim: An agent can resolve a Dataverse contact or lead to a unified customer profile.
claims.quote:
Resolves a unified customer ID from a record identifier in an ingested source system.
Call list_data_sources first to find valid source entity names, such as contact, lead, or a custom table.

claims.claim: Agents can retrieve Customer Insights - Data segment membership for a customer.
claims.quote: Lists the Customer Insights - Data segments or audiences a unified customer belongs to. Each result includes the segment name, display name, and segment ID.

claims.claim: Agents can retrieve calculated customer measures.
claims.quote: Returns calculated customer measures and KPIs, such as lifetime value, order counts, and engagement scores.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Agents can retrieve predictions including churn probability and customer lifetime value.
claims.quote: Returns machine learning predictions for a unified customer, such as churn probability, predicted lifetime value, propensity scores, and next-best-product suggestions.

claims.claim: Agents can retrieve cluster membership, such as a household.
claims.quote: get_cluster_information | Get Cluster Information | Returns cluster membership, such as a household, and other members

claims.claim: Unified profiles combine Dynamics 365 records with external data such as contract or loyalty data.
claims.quote: Customer Insights - Data matches the lead and contact records and creates a unified customer profile that combines Dynamics 365 data with external contract data.

claims.claim: Makers add the server using Tools > Add a tool > MCP, searching for Dynamics 365 CX Customer Insights.
claims.quote:
Go to the Tools page for your agent, and then select Add a tool.
3. Select the MCP filter.
4. Search for Dynamics 365 CX Customer Insights.

claims.claim: Learn documents gateway connections for Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, ChatGPT and Claude Code.
claims.quote: Connect supported external MCP clients, such as Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Claude Code

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The Customer Insights - Data tools are read-only.
claims.quote: create_journey is the only tool that writes data. It isn't read-only, destructive, or idempotent, so calling it twice creates two journeys. Every other tool only reads.

claims.claim: A single MCP server serves Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys.
claims.quote: One MCP server serves both Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys, but each tool works with a specific app.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: create_journey writes a journey record.
claims.quote: Validates a complete journey JSON payload, enriches it, validates the enriched payload again, and then creates the Customer Insights - Journeys journey record.

claims.claim: create_journey is not idempotent and a retry can create a duplicate journey.
claims.quote: It isn't idempotent, so retrying a failed call can create a duplicate journey.

claims.claim: Profile tools read Dataverse virtual entities reflecting live unified customer data.
claims.quote: They read from Dataverse virtual entities, which reflect the live unified customer data that Customer Insights - Data creates, including its segments, measures, predictions, and clusters.

claims.claim: get_customer_details returns source records identifying which source supplied each winning value.
claims.quote: Each source record includes the non-system attributes from the source entity, how those attributes map to unified profile attributes, and a flag that identifies which source contributed the winning value for each unified field.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that these connections allow data to leave the Dynamics 365 FedRAMP High boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling connections between Dynamics 365 and non-Dynamics 365 services, including Microsoft or external services, allows data to leave the Dynamics 365 FedRAMP High boundary.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft asks the tenant administrator to confirm security, compliance, residency and governance requirements before enabling connections.
claims.quote: Before you enable MCP server connections for your organization, your tenant administrator should confirm that these connections meet your data security, compliance, residency, and governance requirements.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tools execute using the calling user's security context.
claims.quote: Authorization is enforced inside the tool logic using the caller's user context.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The MCP server enforces row-level data security.
claims.quote: Row-level security makes sure users only reach data they're authorized to see

claims.claim: Individual tools check entity-specific privileges.
claims.quote: Each tool checks entity-specific privileges, such as read access to consent purposes

claims.claim: The MCP server never implicitly escalates privileges.
claims.quote: The MCP server never escalates privileges implicitly. Tools act as facades and never do anything beyond what the calling user is permitted to do.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Change & support
claims.claim: Tools can be missing when the calling user lacks underlying Dataverse table privileges.
claims.quote: Tools are missing from the agent | The calling user lacks privileges for the underlying Dataverse tables | Check the user's security role privileges.

claims.claim: Connections use OAuth through Agent 365 Tooling Gateway.
claims.quote: Agent 365 Tooling Gateway is an OAuth 2.0-protected resource.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Using the /.default scope requires admin consent granted in advance.
claims.quote: The /.default scope doesn't support incremental or dynamic user consent, so admin consent must be granted in advance in the customer tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can consent to the named McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All permission if tenant user consent is allowed.
claims.quote: If your client requests that named permission instead of /.default, each person can consent for themselves the first time they sign in, as long as your tenant allows user consent for apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: External clients use their own Microsoft Entra client apps, which must be allowed to call the gateway.
claims.quote: Each of these clients signs in with its own Microsoft Entra client app, so a tenant admin still needs to allow that client to call the gateway.

claims.claim: A valid gateway token without the Customer Insights permission can produce 403 Forbidden.
claims.quote: a client can have a valid gateway token and still get 403 Forbidden from the MCP server.

claims.claim: The documented permission diagnostic is to check the token's scp claim for McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All.
claims.quote: If calls are denied, decode the token and check that the scp claim contains McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All.

claims.claim: Omitting /mcp/environments/ from the server URL produces a 404.
claims.quote: The /mcp/environments/ path segment is required. If you leave it out, the request returns 404 RouteNotFound.

claims.claim: Putting a tenant ID in the environment segment can produce 400 EndpointInvalid.
claims.quote: 400 EndpointInvalid, with the message Environment id ... is invalid. | The /environments/ segment holds a tenant ID or a malformed GUID

claims.claim: Each environment has its own server URL and needs its own connector configuration.
claims.quote: The server URL is specific to the environment, so each environment needs its own connector configuration.

claims.claim: Profile lookups require unified Customer Insights - Data profiles.
claims.quote: The customer profile tools, which need Customer Insights - Data, follow a two-step pattern: resolve a unified customer ID, then use that ID to retrieve customer data.

claims.claim: Consent, journey and email tools do not require a unified customer ID.
claims.quote: The consent, journey, and email tools don't need a unified customer ID.

claims.claim: Customer Insights - Data is required for customer profile tools.
claims.quote: For the customer profile tools, Customer Insights - Data.

claims.claim: Consent tools require Customer Insights - Journeys or Shared Consent.
claims.quote: For the consent tools, Customer Insights - Journeys or a Dynamics 365 environment with Shared Consent deployed, for example, Dynamics 365 Sales with Shared Consent.

claims.where: Scope: Users and licences; What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Journey and email tools require Customer Insights - Journeys rather than Customer Insights - Data.
claims.quote: For the journey and email tools, Customer Insights - Journeys.

claims.claim: The System Administrator role is required to configure the MCP server.
claims.quote: The System Administrator role, to configure the MCP server

claims.claim: Manual setup or external-client connection requires tenant admin or delegated admin-consent permissions.
claims.quote: Tenant admin or delegated admin-consent permissions, to set up the server manually or to connect an external MCP client

claims.claim: Catalogue availability follows registration approval and required Microsoft Entra consent.
claims.quote: For MCP servers, registration approval and required Microsoft Entra consent are separate steps. The server becomes available to agent-building surfaces only after consent is granted.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center registry path is Agents > Tools > Registry.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Agents > Tools > Registry.

claims.where: controls[0].note; summary; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Registry Block and Unblock govern supported experiences, not necessarily every product or connected component.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 provides administrative controls for supported tools. Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components. An approval or block doesn't necessarily apply across all products or connected components.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for blocking this registered Customer Insights MCP server is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta Agent 365 tools registry MCP server block unblock API; Agent 365 registry block Graph API MCP. Read Tools overview, gateway setup and Graph API search excerpts; found agent inventory APIs, not a block call for this server.

claims.claim: In Copilot Studio, tool selection is configured using Tools > select the MCP server > Allow all.
claims.quote:
Go to the Tools tab for your agent.
2. Select the MCP server from the list of tools.

A settings page for the MCP server appears.

claims.claim: Makers can turn off Allow all and toggle individual tools for one agent, then Save and Publish.
claims.quote: If you don't want to use all the tools offered by an MCP server, you can selectively turn off MCP server tools directly in your agent.

claims.claim: New server tools stay off when Allow all has been turned off.
claims.quote: When you turn off Allow all, any new tools added to the MCP server are turned off by default.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for an agent's Allow all and individual MCP tool selection is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP Allow all tool selection Dataverse Web API botcomponent Power Platform CLI; Copilot Studio MCP Allow all API. Opened Add tools and resources from an MCP server; read PAC and Dataverse search results; no equivalent setting call found.

claims.claim: New-MgServicePrincipal -AppId "<ATG-app-id>" provisions the gateway service principal.
claims.quote: New-MgServicePrincipal -AppId "<ATG-app-id>"

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The gateway provisioning step is performed by a tenant admin.
claims.quote: As a tenant admin, run one of the following commands.

claims.claim: The gateway page also documents az ad sp create --id <ATG-app-id> for provisioning.
claims.quote: az ad sp create --id <ATG-app-id>

claims.claim: A portal provisioning path for the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway service principal is not yet documented for this setup.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 Tooling Gateway provision service principal Enterprise applications admin center UI; Agent 365 Tooling Gateway service principal portal provision. Opened Customer Insights gateway setup: it prescribes CLI/PowerShell and rejects the gateway admin-consent URL.

claims.claim: On the client app, API permissions > Add a permission > APIs my organization uses > gateway app > McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All > Grant admin consent is documented.
claims.quote:
Go to API permissions, and then select Add a permission.
4. Select APIs my organization uses.
5. Search for the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway app by using the app ID.
6. Add the McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All delegated permission.
7. Select Grant admin consent.

claims.claim: The documented v2.0 admin-consent URL targets the user's own client app with scope <ATG-app-id>/.default.
claims.quote: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<customer-tenant-id>/v2.0/adminconsent?client_id=<your-client-app-id>&scope=<ATG-app-id>/.default&redirect_uri=<redirect-uri-registered-on-your-app>

claims.claim: Gateway provisioning and consent to the client's permission are separate actions.
claims.quote: Run the commands in this section instead. If you set the server up manually, grant admin consent on your own client app, as described later in this article.

claims.claim: The gateway service principal must exist before a client can request a token for it.
claims.quote: Before a client app can request a token for it, the gateway service principal must exist in the customer tenant.

claims.claim: Power Platform connector data policies regulate MCP server access and tools for agents in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Access to MCP servers in Copilot Studio relies on Power Platform connectors for connectivity. This condition means that if a data policy regulates Power Platform connectors, it also regulates access to the MCP server and its tools for your agent.

claims.claim: The documented connection process covers prebuilt Microsoft MCP connectors and servers with configured connections.
claims.quote: The process is the same, whether you're adding prebuilt Microsoft MCP connectors or an MCP server to which you configured a connection.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence; Scope: Users and licences
claims.claim: The feature overview lists access to Dataverse tables as its sole prerequisite and names no MCP server licence there.
claims.quote:
## Prerequisites

The user must have access to the Dataverse tables.

claims.claim: Returned customer data is constrained by Dataverse privileges and row-level security rather than registry or per-agent tool-availability toggles.
claims.quote: Row-level security makes sure users only reach data they're authorized to see

claims.claim: The registry provides Block and Unblock actions for supported items.
claims.quote:
Block | Prevents the selected tool from being used by agents or workflows.
Unblock | Restores access to a previously blocked tool.

claims.claim: Granting admin consent on the client app puts McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All into the tokens that client requests.
claims.quote: Granting admin consent here is what puts McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All into the tokens your client requests.

claims.claim: get_customer_details returns personal profile attributes such as name, email and address.
claims.quote: Core profile attributes, such as name, email, and address, with system columns excluded
